clue.text: Taster with seconds more than sufficient

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for seconds of time
ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A food taster who gets second helpings because there is plenty to go round.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small portion offered to try, just as a free sample is.

clue.text: Put an end to function in school

indicators.note: the function is placed inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: cot is short for cotangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: Bringing a role at a school to a stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to stamp it out and stop it.

clue.text: A term is concocted for expert players

indicators.note: concocted means made up or cooked up, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A school term is invented for talented musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Masters of music, especially renowned conductors and performers, are the experts so titled in Italian plural.

clue.text: Carelessness having cross obscured for those in a congregation?

indicators.note: having introduces what is done to the carelessness word, its cross hidden
obscured means hidden from view, so the cross letter is removed

parts.note: laxity means slackness or carelessness
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A sloppy churchgoer has covered the crucifix for the worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary churchgoers, as opposed to the clergy, are the lay members of a congregation.

clue.text: Item by soldiers? It's laid on trophy

parts.note: a hen lays an egg, so 'it's laid' describes an egg
a cup is a sporting trophy

explanation.surface: Something placed beside troops, perhaps a medal set on a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'soldiers' are thin strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg, so the egg holder sits beside them at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled-egg holder stands at the breakfast table next to the toast strips nicknamed soldiers.

clue.text: Bird round island in my view recalled as a diver

indicators.note: the bird goes round the letter for island

parts.note: the gull is a seabird

indicators.note: being called back means these words are read in reverse

parts.note: 'to me' means in my view or opinion

explanation.surface: Someone recalling a seabird circling an island and plunging into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: This black-and-white auk dives underwater from cliffs to catch fish, so it is a diving seabird.

clue.text: Carpenter at home makes a contribution

parts.note: Chips is a traditional nickname for a ship's carpenter
in means at home

explanation.surface: A woodworker at home gives something to a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip in is an idiom for adding money or a remark to a common effort.

clue.text: Spanish inn? It's found in school area

indicators.note: found in means the piece is placed inside the school word

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
'it' is sex appeal, SA, with the 's standing for 'is'

explanation.surface: A Spanish hostelry located in a school district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a place of learning; it is a group of whales, POD.
explanation.definitionFit: A posada is a traditional inn or lodging house in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: In Sikkim, odd characters go downhill

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth letters of the place name are taken, the odd-numbered ones

explanation.surface: Up in the Himalayan state of Sikkim, strange people head down the slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: To glide down a snowy slope on runners is exactly to travel downhill in sport.

clue.text: Sabotage drink for refreshment in park activity?

indicators.note: refreshment means making new again, so the letters are freshly rearranged

explanation.surface: Spiking a beverage meant to refresh people in a park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Park' suggests a public garden; it is a skate park.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a board on wheels is a typical pastime in a skate park with ramps.

clue.text: Ever irritable after programming what purged data may become?

indicators.note: programming sets things in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A permanently short-tempered coder, worrying about deleted files.
explanation.definitionFit: Deleted data that cannot be recovered is gone for good, lost beyond recovery.

clue.text: Old bishop likes crumbling four-sided pillar

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: crumbling means breaking up, so the letters of likes fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly cleric enjoys decaying ancient monuments.
explanation.definitionFit: An Egyptian-style tapering stone monument has four faces rising to a pyramid point.

clue.text: Endlessly bringing up origin of sweet dried fruit

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the word for bringing up is dropped

parts.note: raising a child is bringing it up

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A parent forever handing out dried fruit as sweets to the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapes dried in the sun become the small dark fruit used in cakes.

clue.text: Bike races in island surroundings, like the Manx?

indicators.note: the island word forms the surroundings, enclosing the races

parts.note: a cay is a small low island or reef
the TT (Tourist Trophy) races are the motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Motorbike racing round an island, which is what the people of the Isle of Man are known for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Manx' seems to mean the Isle of Man's people, tying in with the TT races; it is the tailless Manx cat, so 'like' it means feline.
explanation.definitionFit: Being like a Manx, a breed of cat, is to be cat-like; the word also means spiteful.

clue.text: Stride nervously round Lakeland feature first off — like some climbers?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the trimmed hill word

the first letter is removed

parts.note: fells are the hills of the English Lake District

explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbers' sounds like mountaineers, fitting the Lakeland scene, but means climbing plants; 'nervously' scrambles the stride letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing plants such as roses are often trained on a wooden lattice frame fixed to a wall.

clue.text: Bad risk men met after flying and landing

indicators.note: after a flight, scattering through the air, the letters of these four words land in a new order

explanation.surface: Dodgy characters meeting up after a plane journey as it touches down.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting off a ship or aircraft and coming ashore is the act of landing.

clue.text: Decline in food at reception?

definitions.meaning: a decline or drop, as in prices
a savoury sauce for dunking snacks at a party

explanation.definitionFit: A dip is both a fall in value and a creamy sauce served with crisps at parties.

clue.text: Lights in city and capital erected as a condition

indicators.note: the lights are set inside the other two pieces

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: erected, built upward in a down clue, means the piece is read bottom to top

parts.note: capital as an adjective means excellent, so A1 with the 1 as I
lamps are lights

explanation.surface: Street lights in a city and a nation's capital put up under certain terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a capital city; it is the British adjective for first-rate, giving A1.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dangerous medical disorder of pregnancy marked by seizures, a condition in the medical sense.

clue.text: Award on stage not new in sport

indicators.note: not means the letter for new is left out

parts.note: the Tony is the American award for theatre

explanation.surface: A theatre prize that is not recent for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport with something is to play with it idly, the verb sense of trifling.

clue.text: Standard complaint about one on a railway regarding diet?

parts.note: par is a standard or norm

indicators.note: the complaint word goes about the numeral

parts.note: a lament is a complaint or expression of grief
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A routine grumble about a single train journey and the food served on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' looks like food; it is a legislative assembly, as in the Japanese or historic German Diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Diet is a national legislature, so anything concerning one relates to a legislative body.

clue.text: Temper shown by idiot for all to see over period

parts.note: an ass is a fool
U is the British film classification for universal viewing, fit for everyone
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A fool showing bad temper in public for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like anger; it is a verb meaning to moderate or soothe.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to soften or moderate it, as one eases pain or grief.

clue.text: A figure occupying seat in outburst that's unrestrained

indicators.note: the article and politician go inside the outburst

parts.note: a rant is an angry outburst
an MP, Member of Parliament, occupies a seat in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A politician in the Commons shouting angrily and out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wild and spreading out of control, like rampant inflation, is unchecked.

clue.text: Greek character in tale embroidered for charm

indicators.note: the Greek letter goes inside the rearranged letters
embroidering a story means elaborating it, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek figure in an exaggerated story famed for his charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A small object worn to ward off evil is a lucky talisman or charm.

clue.text: Support for cue kept by thesp I'd erased

indicators.note: kept by means the letters are held within these words

explanation.surface: An actor's prompt was cut, so the cue line is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cue' suggests an actor's prompt; it is a snooker cue, and the rest supporting it has a spider-like frame.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a raised rest with legs, used to bridge over balls, holds the cue.

clue.text: This person enters service with support over papers etc

indicators.note: the personal pronoun goes in between the other two pieces

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: in this clue 'over' signals that the word for support is turned back to front

parts.note: aid means help or support
the setter refers to themself as this person, ME

explanation.surface: The setter goes to church and has back-up with the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers, along with television and radio, make up the means of communication reaching large audiences.

clue.text: Put in a nutshell, it's acceptable to be in depression

indicators.note: the letter for acceptable is placed inside the hollow

parts.note: a sump is a hollow or pit where liquid collects
U means upper-class and so socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Briefly stated, feeling low is perfectly fine.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise is to express something briefly, which is the idiom of putting it in a nutshell.

clue.text: Son to manage range

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: A child gets by over a wide area.
explanation.definitionFit: The extent or reach of something, its breadth of coverage, is its range.

clue.text: Secret affair is in operation after trouble in retreat

indicators.note: the last two pieces come after the reversed one
going back means the word for trouble is written backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
on means working or in operation

explanation.surface: A clandestine romance is under way after troops pulled back in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean an illicit romantic relationship as well as a contact or connection.

clue.text: Spotted animal that won't keep quiet with time in circus outfit?

indicators.note: refusing to keep means the letter for quiet is let go
the letter for time is put in where the dropped letter was

parts.note: the leopard is a big cat with a spotted coat
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A noisy big cat performing in a circus ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobats and trapeze artists in a circus wear the close-fitting one-piece garment.

clue.text: Golf sometimes leads to this surprised expression

definitions.text: Golf sometimes leads to this surprised expression

parts.words: Golf sometimes leads to this surprised expression
parts.note: golf is G in the radio alphabet, and that letter written out as a word is also a cry of surprise

explanation.walkthrough: Golf is G in the phonetic alphabet; spelt out, G is also the exclamation of astonishment, so 'sometimes' the letter leads to the word.

clue.text: Man or woman collecting chief exec to go round part of Oxford?

indicators.note: turning round means the whole construction is read backwards
the name gathers the executive's title inside it

parts.note: Pat is a name used by both men and women
CEO is chief executive officer

explanation.surface: Someone recruiting a company boss to tour a part of the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' suggests the city or university; it is an Oxford shoe, a laced leather style.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a leather shoe, and the reinforced covering over the front of the foot is one of its parts.

clue.text: Torch singer offering something special?

definitions.meaning: a singer of torch songs who sings loudly and powerfully
an informal word for an outstanding thing, a cracker

explanation.surface: A singer of sad love songs giving a remarkable performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a powerful-voiced vocalist and an informal word for an excellent example share the same word.
